title: Neighborhood bands and the failed medical future
summary: He formed kid bands, still assumed he would be a doctor, until fainting while watching his father operate ended the idea.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: Where did you go from there? This would be the early thirties; wouldn't it?

From there I had an interest in playing with other guys, forming bands, and there was a period of finding other neighborhood musicians, kids that knew other kids that played instruments, trying to put together a little band.
You thought of yourself then as from now on a musician?
I might have had an idea that that's what I wanted to do. I don't think I made a firm commitment at that time. I had still been told by my father that I was going
to be a doctor and I didn't question any of this; I just assumed that I was going to be a doctor. That's what I was told I was going to be.
It didn't work out that way.
He was on the right track. There are more doctors who are musicians than anybody else who are musicians. There's an entity between the two. I'm not sure what it is.
You're right; you're absolutely right. I've discovered that too.

As I said, I didn't make a commitment. I didn't know what I was going to do until the day my father took me with him to watch him perform an operation and I was over his shoulder wearing the white gown, the cap and the mask; really fascinated by it and he took out his scalpel and he cut behind the person's ear and peeled the flesh apart and I went backwards and down. When my father came out of the operation looking very pleased, 'How was that son, did you enjoy it?'
I don't think she was as disturbed as he was.
